source_candidates.title: JS Kunisaki Departs Indonesia after Completing International Disaster Relief Activities
provisional_claims: The October 6 MOD release reports that JS Kunisaki departed Kijing Port for Japan after the conclusion of the Indonesia international disaster-relief operation.
The MOD reports that three JGSDF CH-47 helicopters were aboard the departing ship and carried out 56 firefighting missions totaling approximately 280 tons of water released.
caveats: The release describes conclusion and departure on October 6; do not represent the missions as all occurring on October 6.
Do not infer Japanese-Indonesian military cooperation terms or effectiveness beyond the issuing ministry's wording.
This development is not automatically the same incident as Philippines Sanlakas emergency-response exercises.

source_candidates.title: Courtesy call on Defense Minister Koizumi by H. E. Mr. George Glass, the U.S. Ambassador to Japan
provisional_claims: The MOD says Koizumi met U.S. Ambassador George Glass on October 6 and protested a reported robbery-murder incident in Naha, Okinawa.
According to the ministry, the Japanese government called for investigative cooperation, discipline, recurrence-prevention measures, and consideration for the bereaved family.
caveats: The robbery-murder characterization and demands are explicitly attributed to the Japanese Ministry of Defense; no independent criminal-case adjudication is implied.
A separate October 6 McCormick meeting repeats the ministry's protest and is not independent corroboration of the incident.

source_candidates.title: Courtesy call on Minister of Defense Koizumi by U.S. Senator David McCormick
provisional_claims: The ministry says Koizumi received Senator David McCormick on October 6 and voiced intentions to deepen the Japan–U.S. alliance.
The official account also repeats the government's protest and investigative and discipline requests concerning the reported Naha incident.
caveats: This is a separate meeting, but the repeated protest is not a separate criminal incident.
Do not mistake two MOD pages for independent diplomatic or law-enforcement corroboration.

source_candidates.title: Courtesy call on State Minister of Defense Kiyoshi Odawara by the delegation of the U.S. Senator Michael Bennet
provisional_claims: Japan's state minister of defense received Senator Michael Bennet and his delegation on October 5, according to MOD.
The MOD account thanked Bennet for alliance support and repeated Japan's stated concerns over the reported Naha incident.
caveats: Do not assume this meeting resolved the issue or constituted a defense-policy agreement.
Context, not a separate institutional voice or a second Naha incident.

japan_us_alliance_communications.recurring_issue: shared Ministry of Defense protests concerning one reported Naha incident; three distinct diplomatic courtesy calls
